title: Algebraic Equations
summary: Solve linear equations (including those with fractions), equations in which a product of factors equals zero, simple quadratic and exponential equations, change the subject of a formula, and solve word problems.

notes.text: To solve a linear equation: remove brackets, clear fractions by multiplying **every term** by the LCD, collect the variable terms on one side and the constants on the other, and divide by the coefficient. Check by substituting.

notes.title: Worked example 1
steps: (b) Multiply by the LCD $6$: $3x + 2x = 60$, so $5x = 60$ and $x = 12$.

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: When you multiply by the LCD, put brackets around each numerator. $-4(x - 1) = -4x + 4$, not $-4x - 4$. The minus sign in front of a fraction applies to the whole numerator.
If two numbers multiply to give $0$, at least one of them must be $0$. This is the key to solving equations that can be factorised.

items: Get everything on one side so that the other side is $0$.
Set each factor equal to $0$ and solve.

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: Never divide both sides of $x^2 = 4x$ by $x$. That loses the solution $x = 0$. Move everything to one side and factorise instead.
Write both sides as powers of the same base and equate the exponents. For example, $2^{x + 3} = 32 = 2^5$, so $x + 3 = 5$ and $x = 2$.
Changing the subject of a formula
A formula can be rearranged to make a different variable the subject, using the same inverse operations as for solving equations.

notes.title: Worked example 4
notes.problem:
(a) Make $r$ the subject of $C = 2\pi r$.
(b) Make $t$ the subject of $v = u + at$.
(c) The area of a trapezium is $A = \frac{1}{2}(a + b)h$. Make $h$ the subject, and find $h$ when $A = 36$, $a = 5$ and $b = 7$.
steps: (b) Subtract $u$: $v - u = at$. Divide by $a$: $t = \dfrac{v - u}{a}$.

notes.title: Worked example 5: a rectangle
notes.problem: The length of a rectangle is 3 cm more than twice its breadth. Its perimeter is 36 cm. Find its dimensions.
steps: Let the breadth be $b$; the length is $2b + 3$.

notes.title: Worked example 6: a quadratic word problem
notes.problem: The sum of a number and its square is 30. Find the number.

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: In a word problem, check whether both solutions make sense. A length or a number of people cannot be negative, so reject negative answers in those cases.

items: Linear equations: expand, clear fractions with the LCD (using brackets), collect terms, solve, check.
Quadratic equations: make one side zero, factorise, solve each factor. Do not divide by $x$.
Exponential equations: same base, equate exponents.
Change the subject of a formula with inverse operations.
Word problems: define the variable, set up an equation, solve and check that the answer makes sense.

questions.explanation: $x^2 - 4x = 0$ gives $x(x - 4) = 0$, so $x = 0$ is also a solution.
